subtype: Approach: reducing triggers by muting and removing reminders [Action]
passage: Chaitanya, you asked what actually helped, so I'm Ujjwal and I'll be practical. I did three small things in one afternoon. First, I muted her accounts. Not blocked, not an announcement, just quiet. I did not want a scene. Second, I moved all our photos into a folder called "later", not deleted, just out of sight. Third, my usual route to class went past her department, so I started walking around by the library. It added six minutes. No one knew, and I did not tell anyone. It felt slightly silly, like arranging a room so you don't keep bumping into the same chair. But my mornings stopped starting with a jab. Space to heal, I found, is mostly not seeing things.

qa.q: How many extra minutes did the new route to class add?
qa.a: The new route added six minutes.

qa.q: What was Ujjwal feeling about the changes while making them?
qa.a: Ujjwal felt a little silly but determined, comparing it to moving a room so that a chair is not bumped again.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Ujjwal add, and why?
qa.a: Ujjwal could plan something to do in the time that used to go into checking, because removing reminders leaves a gap that something else should fill.

qa.q: How might Chaitanya see Ujjwal's steps?
qa.a: Chaitanya asked what helped and hears three practical steps with no scene, so Chaitanya sees a plan that anyone could copy quietly.

grounding: Shows muting accounts, storing old photos out of sight and changing a route to reduce reminders after a breakup, without any confrontation.
